subject: Clayton to create report outlining AI risks and opportunities as czar: Report
posts:
AI rush bypasses guardrails as DNI Jay Clayton takes the reins to draft risk reports.
Evidence: Executive briefings, competitive urgency, self-regulation.
#Aletheia #AI

The Trump administration appointed DNI Jay Clayton as AI czar to lead a three-month sprint evaluating technology risks and opportunities.
Stated Judgement: (1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Behind the self-regulatory White House accords lies an unbridled race for dominance that sidesteps enforceable safety standards and accountability.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Speed is prioritized over actual safety frameworks, masking institutional gaps behind high-level committee theater.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 4)

- DNI Jay Clayton: FAIL (-0.8, -0.85) — Frames geopolitical race as excuse for weak rules.
- White House Accord: FAIL (-0.7, -0.75) — Relies on voluntary corporate pledges.
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton leads a three-month initiative to outline artificial intelligence risks following industry meetings at the White House.

The Poison:
Voluntary corporate accords create a facade of oversight while locking in competitive dominance without genuine public safety checks.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing administrative appointment (WHO) with actual systemic risk control (HOW). Voluntary pledges replace binding oversight.

Social Physics Analysis:
The administration runs a Smart Selfish Maneuver: using competitive fear ('risk of not being first') as a pretext to avoid binding regulations while projecting preparedness.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map stated safety goals against voluntary corporate self-regulation, it plots straight toward Lesser Evil. (u=-0.75, psi=-0.80).

The Unavoidable Truth: Voluntary corporate accords cannot substitute for enforceable safety standards in critical technologies.

The Unavoidable Lie: Rushing deployment under competitive panic guarantees secure outcomes for the public.

Alethekanon:
Competitive urgency is weaponized to sideline binding safety frameworks. Voluntary accords are administrative smoke and mirrors.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to watch public safety traded for corporate speed. True innovation requires protecting people first, not just racing to cross the finish line.

Brothekanon:
Classic Washington shuffle—handing tech giants a voluntary pledge pad and calling it an AI czar strategy.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth... but store up treasures in heaven." Matthew 6:19-20 FAIL
Chasing earthly supremacy over foundational safety mirrors the folly of building treasures on shifting sand.

Actual Article Body:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will serve as the Trump administration’s AI czar and lead a three-month effort to establish the “risks and opportunities” of the technology.

Clayton, who was largely expected to lead the White House’s recently formed “Super Intelligence Force,” told the Wall Street Journal in an exclusive interview the “risk of not being first is high” as debates about AI policy swirl in Washington. His appointment comes less than a week after the nation’s leading AI executives convened at the White House and signed a non-binding commitment to self-regulation called the “White House Accord on Super Intelligence.”
